rule.LW-001.name: Brute force
rule.LW-001.description: Many failed logins from a single source IP in a short time window.
rule.LW-001.action: Block or rate-limit the source IP (e.g. fail2ban), check that the targeted accounts use strong passwords or keys, and disable password authentication for SSH if possible.
rule.LW-002.name: Password spraying
rule.LW-002.description: One source IP tries many different accounts, usually with a few common passwords.
rule.LW-002.action: Block the source IP, review the list of targeted accounts, enforce MFA and check for any successful login from this IP.
rule.LW-003.name: Success after failures
rule.LW-003.description: A successful login preceded by repeated failures from the same IP: the password may have been guessed.
rule.LW-003.action: Treat as a possible account compromise: contact the user, reset the password, terminate active sessions and review what the account did after logging in.
rule.LW-004.name: Off-hours login
rule.LW-004.description: A successful login outside business hours or on a weekend.
rule.LW-004.action: Confirm with the user that the login was legitimate. If it was not, handle it as a compromised account.
rule.LW-005.name: Suspicious IP
rule.LW-005.description: A source IP that triggered several different rules or tried several non-existent accounts.
rule.LW-005.action: Block the IP at the perimeter and search other logs (firewall, web, VPN) for activity from it.
